artifact.status_search_result: Density of metrics with positive topological entropy is known on surfaces (Contreras–Paternain established it on $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$ in the $C^2$ topology, and Contreras showed $C^2$-genericity of a non-trivial hyperbolic basic set on any closed manifold), but the analogous statements in higher $C^k$ topologies and for all closed manifolds remain open due to the absence of a closing lemma for geodesic flows. Density of transitive geodesic flows in dimension $\geq 3$ and density of metrics with closed geodesics dense in $SM$ remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Genericity of geodesic flows with positive topological entropy on S^2
status_evidence.snippet: The set of C^infty Riemannian metrics on S^2 (and RP^2) whose geodesic flow has positive topological entropy is C^2 open and dense.
status_evidence.claim: Question (i) is solved on S^2 and RP^2 in the C^2 topology.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic flows with positive topological entropy, twist maps and hyperbolicity
status_evidence.snippet: On any closed manifold, a C^2-generic Riemannian metric has a non-trivial hyperbolic basic set in its geodesic flow; the lack of a closing lemma prevents extension to higher C^k.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-regularity and full generality remain open.
